correctness.rationale: For qubits, the pair subvector in the defining Eq. (31) has a single local-generator component and its squared norm is \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{ij}\widetilde{\rho}_{ij})\). The two-qubit spin-flip identity converts this to \(1-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_i^2)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_j^2)+\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{ij}^2)\); global purity replaces \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{ij}^2)\) by \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_k^2)\), giving \((T_i+T_j-T_k)/2\). The three CKW equalities then give \(c_{ij}^2+\tau/2\). Summation gives \(3Q/2\). GHZ, W, and Bell-pair-product boundary cases match the defining source exactly.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact structural interpretation of a published pair-labelled quantity: every pair receives precisely half of the genuine three-tangle, explaining why GHZ has nonzero pair labels despite zero reduced-pair concurrence. It also identifies the total scalar exactly with a fixed rescaling of Meyer-Wallach \(Q\), so on pure three qubits it provides no independent scalar ordering. This sharp boundary is mathematically motivated by the source's stated pairwise interpretation.
